text: Which Hebridean stone circle on the Isle of Lewis, shaped like a Celtic cross, is more than 4,000 years old?
info: Callanish, on the west coast of Lewis, in the Outer Hebrides.

text: Which Wiltshire village sits inside the largest stone circle in Britain?
info: Avebury, in Wiltshire; the circle surrounds part of the village.

text: Which huge man-made chalk mound, the tallest prehistoric one in Europe, stands near Avebury?
info: Silbury Hill, beside the A4 near Avebury; about 4,400 years old.

text: Which Oxfordshire palace, built for the Duke of Marlborough, was the birthplace of Winston Churchill?
info: Blenheim Palace, at Woodstock in Oxfordshire.

text: Which moated Kent castle has been called 'the loveliest castle in the world'?
info: Leeds Castle, near Maidstone in Kent; it has nothing to do with Leeds in Yorkshire.

text: Which West Sussex castle is the home of the Duke of Norfolk?
Which Somerset cave system, home to the 'Witch of Wookey', is also a tourist attraction with a papermill?
info: Wookey Hole, near Wells in Somerset.

text: Which East Lothian harbour town was the birthplace of John Muir, the 'father of national parks'?
info: Dunbar, on the East Lothian coast; Muir emigrated to America as a boy.
